Consult Summary:
- 26-year-old woman presenting with a worsening, right-sided headache for three days, associated with photophobia and visual disturbances, unresponsive to Ibuprofen, likely migraine.

History:
- Presenting Complaint: Headache for three days, worsening over time.
- Onset/Timeline: Began three days ago, started at work with gradual development; worsened the next morning and has since intensified.
- Progression: Persisting and increasing in severity over three days; currently rated 8/10.
- Nature of pain: Dull, sometimes sharper, all over head but mainly around right eye.
- Duration: Persistent, but with fluctuating intensity.
- Exacerbating/Relieving Factors: Tried Ibuprofen for past two days (three tablets a day); did not relieve headache (previously effective, not effective this time). Reducing screen brightness for work.
- Associated Symptoms:
    - Photophobia (“light is quite annoying, hurts to look at bright lights”)
    - Visual disturbances (“weird shooting lights” at onset, no loss of vision)
    - Mild nausea (“feel sick with the headache,” no vomiting)
    - Difficulty focusing, had to take days off work
- Pertinent Negatives:
    - No neck pain or stiffness
    - No speech difficulties
    - No limb weakness
    - No fevers, rashes, recent head injury
    - No prior headaches of similar severity or duration (previous headaches resolved with Ibuprofen)
- Family history notable for migraines in mother and sister

Past Medical History:
- No chronic medical conditions reported
- No personal history of migraines

Medications:
- Ibuprofen, dose/route/frequency: 3 tablets/day (specific dose per tablet not documented)
- No regular medications
- No known medication allergies

Social History:
- Lives with three housemates
- Works in IT; computer/screen-based work exacerbates symptoms
- Wears glasses (since age 5); last eye check not recent
- Reports some stress at work (new project), but not out of the ordinary
- Social smoker
- Drinks alcohol socially

Family History:
- Mother: Frequent migraines (“quite bad,” triggered by season changes, can incapacitate for days)
- Sister: Migraines, rare/occasional

Physical Examination:
- Not documented

Investigations:
- None performed or reported

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Suspected migraine headache
  - Assessment:
    - Headache worsening over three days, right-sided predominance, photophobia, visual disturbance, family history of migraine, and poor response to simple analgesia suggest migraine.
  - Plan:
    - Educated patient on appropriate dosing of Ibuprofen (up to 2 tablets, 3x daily).
    - Offer prescription for stronger analgesia: options discussed include Naproxen, Paracetamol, and Codeine (dose/route/frequency not documented).
    - Recommended keeping a headache diary to identify potential triggers.
    - Advised follow-up in 1–2 weeks or sooner if symptoms persist or worsen.
    - If more frequent episodes occur, discussion of migraine prophylaxis at next visit.
    - Advised to seek prompt review if experiencing new vision problems, limb weakness, or general decline.

General Plan:
- Consider repeat eye test if visual symptoms or eye strain persist.
- Maintain low screen brightness as symptom control.
